comments.author: CarthagoFuckYourself
comments.body:
I mean, whether I'd go so far as to say you made if depends on what your workflow was. It's a bit pretentious to say you made it if the only thing that went into it was prompt engineering.


I find you get a lot less pushback if you very intentionally include documentation of an sketches you made and reference images used while prompting. Even then, I still find it's rhetorically helpful to say generated instead of made even if both are technically accurate. You won't convince some blind haters out there, but giving people a peek behind the curtain is part of winning the optics war around AI use.

replies.author: StupidCodeGenerator
replies.body: Thank you for your constructive feedback.

comments.author: Technical-Pin7028
comments.body:
Good evening. I am the one who said that Gemini made this art, not you. If you had responded to me directly instead of doing a spite post, I would have said the following in the first place:

The reason I do not believe you made this art is because all you do for making AI art is give it a prompt, and it gives you art. You can technically argue that there is effort that is put into the prompt. However, I offer you this example as rebuttal: if I were to go to an artist, and commission them to draw one of my OCs, did I make the art that they produce? No. I cannot, and should not, claim that I am the one that made the art.

The process of commissioning is the same as the process of ai. You give a request, provide payment, and in return you receive a good. You have the right to own and use that good, but you are not the one responsible for making it.
